mainTopic: Blood found in the פרוזדור: ספק or ודאי, and אביי's two approaches (worry vs. חזקה)
overview: The amud opens with the last words of the earlier topic: a כלי חרס makes everything in its airspace טמא, even if it is full of mustard seeds. Then a new משנה pictures a woman's body as a house with a חדר, a פרוזדור and an עלייה. Blood from the חדר is טמא, blood from the עלייה is טהור, and blood found in the פרוזדור is טמא because we presume it came from the מקור. In the גמרא, students describe the layout and say there is a לול, an opening, between the עלייה and the פרוזדור. רב הונא then explains that blood found from the לול inward is ודאי טמא, and blood from the לול outward is ספקו טמא. אביי objects that a woman's change in posture could move blood in either direction. So he says we must choose one approach: follow the worry, and both places are a ספק, or follow the חזקה, and inside is ודאי טמא while outside is ודאי טהור. Finally, the גמרא matches these two options to an argument between רבי חייא and רב קטינא about whether blood in the פרוזדור is definitely impure. The discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing line of the previous discussion: even a vessel full of mustard seeds
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the earlier sugya: everything inside a כלי חרס becomes טמא, even if the vessel is packed with mustard seeds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if it is full of mustard seeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the discussion from before this section. It says that a כלי חרס makes everything inside its airspace טמא, even if the vessel is completely full of tiny mustard seeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a כלי חרס, טומאה depends on the airspace inside the vessel, not on touching. So even tiny seeds that never touch the walls or the source of טומאה still become טמא. This line closes that topic before the new משנה starts.

keyTerms.meaning: Mustard seed, a classic example of something very tiny
Full
Even

phrases.english: Even if it is full of mustard seeds.
phrases.notes: This wraps up the earlier topic. The 'it' is a כלי חרס, and the air inside it makes everything in it טמא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the sugya from before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The airspace of a כלי חרס makes all its contents טמא, even tiny mustard seeds packed inside it.

steps.title: The משנה's parable: a woman's body as a house
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes a woman's body using the picture of a house with three parts: the חדר, the פרוזדור, and the עלייה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The חכמים gave a parable about a woman: the room, the corridor, and the upper story.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. The חכמים use the picture of a house to describe three parts of a woman's body. This sets up the rulings in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of the house stands for a body part. The חדר is the uterus, the פרוזדור is the passage leading to it, and the עלייה is the bladder. Naming these parts lets the משנה rule on blood depending on where it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable or comparison
Inner room; here, the uterus
Corridor or entrance passage; here, the vaginal canal
Upper story; here, the bladder

steps.confusionAlert: The house is only a picture. The rulings are about real body parts: חדר is the uterus, פרוזדור is the passage, and עלייה is the bladder.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: The Sages stated a parable about a woman:
the room, and the corridor, and the upper story.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic begins with a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman's body is described as a house with three parts: חדר, פרוזדור, and עלייה.

steps.title: Which blood is impure, which is pure, and what about the corridor
steps.stepSummary: Blood from the חדר is טמא and blood from the עלייה is טהור. Blood found in the פרוזדור is treated as טמא, because we assume it came from the מקור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blood of the room is impure. Blood of the upper story is pure. If blood is found in the corridor, even though there is a doubt, it is impure, because we assume it came from the source.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the rulings for each part of the 'house'. It also explains what to do when blood is found in the corridor and we don't know where it came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood from the uterus makes a woman טמא, while blood from the bladder does not. Blood found in the פרוזדור could have come from either place. The משנה rules it טמא because of a חזקה that blood there normally comes from the מקור.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually impure
Ritually pure
Its doubtful case
Its presumed status (חזקה)
The 'source', meaning the uterus

steps.whatToRemember: חדר blood is טמא, עלייה blood is טהור, and פרוזדור blood is טמא because we presume it came from the מקור.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule in הלכות נדה. A doubt about where blood came from is decided by a חזקה, not by leniency.

phrases.english: Blood of the room is impure,
blood of the upper story is pure,
if it was found in the corridor, its doubtful case is impure,
because its presumption is that it came from the source.
phrases.notes: 'The source' means the uterus, which is the חדר of the parable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the parable from the previous line to give actual rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חדר blood is טמא. עלייה blood is טהור. Blood found in the פרוזדור is טמא, because it is presumed to come from the מקור.

steps.title: Two students explain the layout of the 'house'
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר שמואל and רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה were learning מסכת נדה at רב הונא's study hall. רבה בר רב הונא found them describing the layout: the חדר is inside, the פרוזדור is outside, the עלייה is above both, and a לול opens between the עלייה and the פרוזדור.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רמי בר שמואל and רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה were learning מסכת נדה in the study hall of רב הונא. רבה בר רב הונא found them sitting and saying: The room is inside, the corridor is outside, the upper story is built over both of them, and an opening connects the upper story and the corridor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about two students who were explaining how the parts of the 'house' are arranged. This sets up the next move, which is what רבה בר רב הונא says to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students add details the משנה did not give: which part is inside, which is outside, and that the עלייה sits above both. They also say there is an open passage, a לול, between the עלייה and the פרוזדור. That explains how bladder blood could reach the פרוזדור and create the doubt in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: They were learning or reviewing
He found them
On the inside / on the outside
A small open passage or opening
Built, situated

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rami bar Shmuel
and Rav Yitzchak, son of Rav Yehuda,
were learning Niddah in the study hall of Rav Huna.
Rabba bar Rav Huna found them
sitting and saying:
the room is on the inside, and the corridor is on the outside,
and the upper story is built over both of them,
and an opening is open between the upper story and the corridor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא דְּיָתְבִי וְקָאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה by describing the physical layout of the parts in its parable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חדר is inside, the פרוזדור is outside, the עלייה is above both, and a לול connects the עלייה to the פרוזדור.

steps.title: The students' rule: inside the opening is doubtful-impure, outside is doubtful-pure
steps.stepSummary: The students teach that blood found from the לול inward is ספקו טמא, and from the לול outward is ספקו טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If blood is found from the opening (the לול) and further in, we are unsure where it came from, and we treat it as טמא. If it is found from the opening and further out, we are unsure, and we treat it as טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: We are still hearing what רבה בר רב הונא heard the students saying. They give a rule that depends on where the blood was found compared to the לול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לול is the opening between the עלייה and the פרוזדור. Blood found deeper than it is more likely from the חדר, so the doubt goes to טמא. Blood found past it is more likely from the עלייה, so the doubt goes to טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: The opening that connects the עֲלִיָּיה to the פְּרוֹזְדוֹר
From the opening and further inside
From the opening and further outside
Its doubt is ruled impure: we are unsure, but treat it as טָמֵא
Its doubt is ruled pure: we are unsure, but treat it as טָהוֹר

steps.confusionAlert: Note the word ספקו. The students are not saying the blood is definitely טמא. They are saying it is a doubt that we rule טמא. That one word sets up the next challenge.

phrases.english: If it was found from the opening and inward
its doubt is impure;
from the opening and outward
its doubt is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא מִן הַלּוּל וְלִפְנִים סְפֵקוֹ טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the report of what the students in רב הונא's בית מדרש were saying, applying the house layout from step 4 to the ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood from the לול inward is ספקו טמא; from the לול outward is ספקו טהור.

steps.title: The son asks: how can it be a doubt if the משנה calls it a presumption?
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא asks his father רב הונא how he could call the inside blood a ספק, when the משנה says it has a חזקה of coming from the מקור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came and said to his father: Did you, Master, tell us that its doubt is טמא? But we learned in the משנה: 'because its presumption is that it comes from the מקור'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא goes to his father and challenges the rule he heard. He points out that the משנה's wording does not sound like a doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says blood in the פרוזדור is טמא because of a חזקה that it came from the מקור. A חזקה means we treat it as definitely from the מקור, not as an unsure case. So calling it ספקו טמא seems to clash with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A presumption; we treat something as a set fact unless shown otherwise
The source, meaning the womb (the חֶדֶר)
Master, a respectful way of saying 'you'
But look! A word that opens a challenge

phrases.english: He came and said to his father:
phrases.notes: This is רבה בר רב הונא, going to his father רב הונא.

phrases.english: Did the Master tell us that its doubt is impure?
But we learned: "because its presumption is that it is from the source"!
phrases.notes: He is quoting the משנה from step 3, about blood found in the פרוזדור.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְפֵקוֹ טָמֵא אֲמַרְתְּ לַן מָר? וְהָא אֲנַן שֶׁחֶזְקָתוֹ מִן הַמָּקוֹר תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule in step 5 by comparing it to the משנה's wording in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that blood from the לול inward is only ספקו טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives the blood a חזקה of coming from the מקור, which means definite impurity. A ruling of mere doubt contradicts that.

steps.title: רב הונא clarifies: inside is definitely impure, outside is doubtful-impure
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains he was misquoted. Blood from the לול inward is ודאי טמא; blood from the לול outward is ספקו טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I said. From the opening and inward, it is definitely טמא. From the opening and outward, its doubt is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers his son by correcting what the students said in his name. He moves each case one level stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the inside blood is ודאי טמא, which matches the משנה's חזקה. The outside blood, which the students called ספקו טהור, is now ספקו טמא. So the משנה's case is the inside blood, and the outside blood is a separate, doubtful case.

keyTerms.meaning: Definitely impure, with no doubt
This is what I was saying, used to correct a misunderstanding

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's final position: from the לול inward is ודאי טמא (the משנה's חזקה), and from the לול outward is ספקו טמא.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I said:
from the opening and inward, it is definitely impure;
from the opening and outward, its doubt is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 by restating the rule in a way that fits the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the original statement: the students got it wrong.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The inside blood was only ספקו טמא, which clashed with the משנה's חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The inside blood is ודאי טמא, which matches the משנה; the outside blood is ספקו טמא.

steps.title: אביי asks: if outside blood might be from the חדר, inside blood might be from the עלייה
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the reason for treating outside blood as ספקו טמא would also make inside blood only a doubt, not ודאי טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Why is blood found from the opening outward treated as doubtful-impure? Because maybe she bent forward and it came from the חדר. Then from the opening inward too, say: maybe she leaned back and it came from the עלייה!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב הונא's clarification from step 7. He says the same kind of 'maybe' works in both directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside blood is ספקו טמא only because the woman might have bent forward, letting blood from the חדר reach the outer area. But by that logic she might also have leaned back, letting blood from the עלייה reach the inner area. If so, the inside blood should also be just a doubt, not ודאי טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? Used to argue two cases should be treated the same
Perhaps, maybe
She bent forward
She straightened up or leaned back
The upper story (the bladder area), whose blood is טָהוֹר

phrases.english: Abaye said: What is different
about from the opening and outward, that its doubt is impure?
Because perhaps she bent over, and it came from the room.
From the opening and inward too, say:
she leaned back, and it came from the upper story!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא מִן הַלּוּל וְלַחוּץ דִּסְפֵקוֹ טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's answer in step 7 by showing its reasoning applies equally to the inside case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that blood from the לול inward is ודאי טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a change in posture (bending forward) can make outside blood possibly from the חדר, then a change in posture (leaning back) can make inside blood possibly from the עלייה. Then the inside case should also be only a ספק.

steps.title: אביי's consistent rule: either both are doubtful, or both are definite
steps.stepSummary: אביי says we must be consistent. If we follow the worry, blood both inside and outside the לול is a ספק. If we follow the חזקה, inside is ודאי טמא and outside is ודאי טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: If you follow the worry, both cases are a doubt. If you follow the presumption, from the לול inward is definitely impure, and from the לול outward is definitely pure.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now gives his own answer to the problem he raised. He says you cannot mix the two approaches, so you have to pick one and apply it to both places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8 אביי showed that רב הונא's version was inconsistent: it used the worry for the outside but ignored it for the inside. Here he offers two clean options. Using the worry makes both places a ספק. Using the חזקה makes both places definite, one impure and one pure.

keyTerms.meaning: A worry or concern; here, the worry that the blood moved from where it started
A presumption based on what is normally true
This one and that one, meaning both cases
Definitely pure
You go after, meaning you follow a certain principle

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's two options: follow the worry, and both places are a ספק. Follow the חזקה, and inside is ודאי טמא while outside is ודאי טהור.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
If you go after the worry,
phrases.notes: He means the worry that the blood may have shifted from the place it first came to.

phrases.english: then this one and that one are both a doubt;
and if you go after the presumption,
then from the opening inward it is definitely impure,
and from the opening outward it is definitely pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the inconsistency אביי raised in step 8 by giving two consistent options.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: offers two internally consistent approaches in place of the mixed one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Inside blood could be ודאי טמא while outside blood is only ספקו טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Either both places are a ספק, or inside is ודאי טמא and outside is ודאי טהור.

steps.title: רבי חייא and רב קטינא argue about blood in the corridor
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that blood found in the פרוזדור is treated as definitely impure, for entering the מקדש and for burning תרומה. רב קטינא says it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: Blood found in the פרוזדור makes one liable for entering the מקדש, and we burn תרומה because of it. רב קטינא said: One is not liable for entering the מקדש because of it, and we do not burn תרומה because of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching of רבי חייא and the disagreeing view of רב קטינא about blood found in the פרוזדור. This sets up the next steps, which connect it to אביי's two options.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being liable for entering the מקדש and burning תרומה only happen when the impurity is definite. So רבי חייא treats this blood as ודאי טמא, while רב קטינא treats it as only a ספק.

keyTerms.meaning: Entering the Temple while impure
Burning תרומה because it became definitely impure
One is liable because of it

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree there is some impurity. They argue only about whether it is definite (רבי חייא) or doubtful (רב קטינא).

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya taught:
Blood that is found in the corridor:
one is liable because of it for entering the Temple,
and we burn תרומה because of it.
phrases.notes: תרומה is burned only when its impurity is certain, so this means the blood counts as definitely impure.

phrases.english: And Rav Ketina said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו עַל בִּיאַת מִקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: one is not liable because of it for entering the Temple,
and we do not burn תרומה because of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new disagreement that the גמרא will connect to אביי's two options.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא: blood in the פרוזדור is ודאי טמא. רב קטינא: it is only ספק טמא.

steps.title: אביי's worry option supports רב קטינא
steps.stepSummary: Under אביי's first option, following the worry, blood in the canal is only a ספק. That matches רב קטינא and goes against רבי חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the version where אביי said 'If you follow the worry,' this supports רב קטינא and disagrees with רבי חייא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lines up אביי's first option with the argument in step 10. If we follow the worry, the blood is a doubt, which is exactly what רב קטינא says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry option makes all blood in the canal a ספק. רב קטינא's ruling, no liability for the מקדש and no burning of תרומה, fits a doubt. רבי חייא, who treats it as definite, does not fit this option.

keyTerms.meaning: Version or way of saying something; here, one of אביי's two options
It supports him
It disagrees with

phrases.english: According to that version that Abaye said:
"If you go after the worry,"
it supports Rav Ketina,
and it disagrees with Rabbi Chiya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects אביי's first option from step 9 to the argument in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רב קטינא's view that blood in the פרוזדור is only a ספק
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's first option, following the worry

steps.title: אביי's presumption option supports רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: Under אביי's second option, following the חזקה, blood inside the לול is definitely impure. That matches רבי חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the version where you said 'If you follow the presumption,' this supports רבי חייא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now lines up אביי's second option with רבי חייא. If we follow the חזקה, inside blood is ודאי טמא, so liability for the מקדש and burning תרומה make sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the חזקה option, blood from the לול inward is definite impurity. רבי חייא's strict rulings need definite impurity, so this option supports him, as long as he is talking about blood found on the inside part.
steps.whyThisMatters: Together, steps 11 and 12 show that the argument between רבי חייא and רב קטינא matches exactly the choice between אביי's two options.

phrases.english: According to that version that you said:
"If you go after the presumption,"
it supports Rabbi Chiya,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 11, now matching אביי's second option to רבי חייא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חייא's view that blood in the פרוזדור is ודאי טמא
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's second option, following the חזקה
